pascal.name: Blaise Pascal
pascal.summary: At age sixteen published the broadsheet Essay pour les coniques (1640) announcing the Hexagrammum Mysticum (Pascal's Theorem), generalizing Pappus's two-line lemma to any smooth conic section.

desargues.name: Girard Desargues
desargues.role: French geometer and architect, founder of projective geometry
desargues.summary: Pioneered synthetic projective geometry and points at infinity in his 1639 Brouillon project; acknowledged by young Pascal as the primary inspiration for his conic methods.

pappus.name: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus.role: Alexandrian geometer and author of the Synagoge (Mathematical Collection)
pappus.summary: Proved the two-line Hexagon Theorem (Synagoge VII.139) thirteen centuries before Pascal generalized it to smooth conics.

apollonius.name: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius.role: The Great Geometer of antiquity and author of the Conics
apollonius.summary: Established the classical theory of conics as planar sections of a cone, providing the foundation that Desargues and Pascal transformed projectively.

steiner.name: Jakob Steiner
steiner.role: Swiss geometer and master of synthetic projective geometry
steiner.summary: Discovered in 1828 that the 60 Pascal lines concur three-by-three at 20 Steiner points (two per complementary triangle partition).

pluecker.name: Julius Plücker
pluecker.summary: Discovered in 1830 that the 20 Steiner points lie four-by-four along 15 Plücker lines, establishing line coordinates and projective duality.

kirkman.name: Thomas Penyngton Kirkman
kirkman.summary: Discovered in 1850 that the 60 Pascal lines concur three-by-three in a second way at 60 Kirkman points, three of which lie on each Pascal line.

chasles.name: Michel Chasles
chasles.role: French geometer and historian of mathematics
chasles.summary: Proved that four points on an irreducible conic possess an intrinsic cross-ratio independent of the observer point on the conic (Traité des sections coniques, 1865).

brianchon.name: Charles Julien Brianchon
brianchon.summary: Discovered in 1806 Brianchon's theorem, the exact projective dual of Pascal's theorem: the three principal diagonals of a circumscribed hexagon concur at a single point.

mersenne.name: Marin Mersenne, O.M.
mersenne.role: French polymath and central node of the European scientific correspondence
mersenne.summary: Organized the Paris mathematical academy attended by Desargues, Fermat, and Étienne & Blaise Pascal; distributed Pascal's 1640 broadside to Descartes.

leibniz.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
leibniz.role: German philosopher and polymath, co-inventor of the calculus
leibniz.summary: Examined Pascal's unpublished manuscript treatise on conics (Genera Conicorum) in Paris in 1676 at the request of Pascal's heirs, copying key extracts before the manuscript was lost.
